terms.gloss: One of the cards set aside face down during setup; a player takes one for each Knock Out and wins by taking them all.
The resource an attack costs, supplied by Energy cards attached to a Pokemon; each carries a type that printed costs are matched against.
The elemental kind of a Pokemon or an Energy card, matched against attack costs and read for Weakness and Resistance.
A power printed on a Pokemon card that is not an attack; usually optional, once per turn, and switched off while the Pokemon carries a Special Condition.
terms.glyph_note: Red follows the cards, which print ABILITY as a red banner. Not a semantic negative.

terms.gloss: A card played on top of a Pokemon already in play, and the stage line such cards form.
The in-play spot a Pokemon fights from, and the Pokemon standing in it; only that Pokemon can attack or carry a Special Condition.
A suffix forming part of a card's name that marks a stronger Pokemon giving up extra Prize cards when Knocked Out; the older line spells it -EX.
A card variant with higher HP and stronger attacks than the plain version of the same name, worth two Prize cards when Knocked Out.
A suffix forming part of a card's name that marks a Pokemon-GX, which carries a once-per-game GX attack and a marker to record it as spent.
The expansion a card was released in, read together with its collector number when a deck is checked against a deck list.
Everything live in a game at one moment: both boards, both hands, and the choices open to each player.
Short for Special Condition: Asleep, Burned, Confused, Paralyzed or Poisoned, carried by the Active Pokemon until something clears it.
Take a Pokemon out of play once its damage reaches its HP; the Pokemon is Knocked Out and its opponent takes a Prize card.
Take the top card of your deck into your hand; every turn opens with one, and being unable to draw loses the game.
Put a card from hand or from play into its owner's discard pile.
Take something off a Pokemon or out of play, such as a Special Condition, an attached card or a marker.
Place further damage counters on a Pokemon, as Burned and Confused do, or fold a bonus into damage already being worked out.
Marks a cost, effect or trait as what the card itself shows, rather than what it has become through an effect in play.
A fresh game played when both players would win at the same moment; the first to take a Prize card takes the match.
